memory_candidates.content: A bare `[ cond ] && action` as the LAST statement of a bash while-loop body under `set -e` silently aborts the whole script the moment `cond` is false on the final line of input -- the short-circuited list's nonzero exit status propagates to the enclosing context. This is insulated (harmless) when the loop producing/consuming the data runs inside a process-substitution subshell (`done < <(producer)`), because the subshell's death coincides with the pipe's own natural EOF and nothing downstream checks its exit code -- but calling the SAME function directly in the caller's own shell (e.g. to let a sibling function read a populated associative array afterward) removes that accidental insulation and the crash becomes real and silent (exit 1, zero stdout/stderr, no error message). Always use explicit `if`/`then` instead of a bare `&&`-guarded action as a loop's last statement when the guard can legitimately be false on real data's last record.

This repository's shell-test-suite common.sh (`common_test_resolve_subject`) defaults subject resolution to `deploy-tree-first`: it silently resolves and copies the STALE deployed `.claude/scripts/` copy ahead of a source-store edit whenever both exist, by design (so a pre/post-redeploy run pair produces the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint's divergence signal). For a multi-phase task whose plan edits the source store with redeploy deferred to a final phase, every intermediate phase's own `run-all.sh --only SUITE` verification must export `CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store` to actually validate the edits being made -- otherwise the check silently passes by testing pre-edit behavior, producing false-confidence (not necessarily a false PASS, but an unearned one) until the final redeploy phase makes the two trees identical again.

check-extension-docs.sh's INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE (governing Rule R, index-entries.json line_count accuracy) defaults to 'hard', not advisory -- a direct invocation (or verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 3,4) genuinely exits 1 on a declared-but-not-yet-reconciled line_count drift. 'Rule R is advisory here (no pre-commit hook installed)' -- a framing that appears in plan-authoring guidance for a source-store-edit task that defers index-entries.json reconciliation to a later redeploy phase -- is true only for git commits (no pre-commit hook invokes this script); it does NOT mean the script's own default gate mode is lenient. Export INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE=advisory to confirm no OTHER finding exists beneath an expected, declared drift before a later phase's redeploy reconciles it.

sapience_notes.subject: orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh build_ready_set()
sapience_notes.value: A latent set -e crash: `[ "$all_ok" = true ] && READY_SET["$task_num"]=1` as a while-loop's last statement silently aborts the script (exit 1, zero output) when the LAST line read has all_ok=false. It was harmless pre-refactor because it ran inside a process-substitution subshell; became live-crashing once the shell had to run directly so a sibling function could see the populated array. Fixed with if/then.

sapience_notes.subject: this repository's shell-test common_test_resolve_subject()
sapience_notes.value: Its default deploy-tree-first mode silently resolves the stale deployed .claude/scripts/ copy ahead of a source-store edit whenever both exist. A multi-phase implementation task editing the source store with redeploy deferred to a final phase must export CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store on every intermediate verification run, or the check tests pre-edit behavior without any visible warning.

sapience_notes.subject: check-extension-docs.sh's INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE
sapience_notes.value: Defaults to 'hard', not advisory -- contradicting a common plan-authoring framing ('Rule R is advisory here, no pre-commit hook installed') that conflates 'no git pre-commit hook blocks this' with 'the script's own default gate mode is lenient'. A direct invocation genuinely exits 1 on a declared, not-yet-reconciled index-entries.json line_count drift.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh's internal verification call
sapience_notes.value: Runs verify-deploy.sh with --skip-slow automatically as part of normal deploy operation, deferring gate 8 (the shell test suite) regardless of any batch-gate-deferral directive -- this is deploy-headless.sh's own standing default, not something a dispatch has to request. A phase requiring the full test suite result must separately run the scoped run-all.sh --only invocation.

sapience_notes.subject: build_ready_set() and roadmap-integration.sh's render_next()
sapience_notes.value: Both implement the same readiness concept (is this task still something to act on, or has it already finished) at two different bars for two different purposes -- build_ready_set()'s bar is stricter (also excludes hold/implementing/blocked/partial). They are deliberately not unified into one shared function since no live caller needs both bars at once; a future change to one terminal-status filter should prompt checking the other.
